subject: Post-call TCO recap — token levers, batching & caching, and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Miles <evan.miles@paygate.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call TCO recap — token levers, batching & caching, and pilot next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today, Evan — good conversation. Below is a concise recap + recommended next steps so your team has a single place to reference. I copied Soojin (solutions) and Marissa (AE) so we can move to a pilot/quote quickly.

TL;DR (for execs): Your current LLM spend for the customer-facing flows is estimated at $22k/month. With Redwood’s batching, prefix/KV caching, and a modest quantization profile, we estimate a 35–55% reduction in unit inference cost in a 90-day pilot (conservative case ~38%). Pilot budget ask: $9k/mo (net of credits) for the initial 60-day run to prove savings and latency retention.

Key pain points you shared:
- High and unpredictable per-message spend tied to peak-hour traffic spikes (~1.2M tokens/day).
- Latency SLOs: sub-300ms 95th for single-utterance prompts (must remain under 350ms).
- Experiments with local caching made quality regressions for some dialog contexts.
- Procurement needs: clear cost model and an easy rollback path.

Goals we aligned on:
1) Validate a 30–50% unit-cost reduction without increasing 95th latency beyond +50ms.
2) Surface deterministic monthly spend for finance and procurement (a committed pilot SKU + overage model).
3) Define operational runbook (alerts, fallback to cheaper variant, basic audit logs).

Estimated lever breakdown (illustrative):
- Continuous batching & dynamic batching window tuning: 12–18% savings (best in bursty payment flows).
- Prefix/KV caching on repeated intents: 10–25% savings depending on cache hit rates (we'll instrument hit-rate dashboards).
- Lower-precision model variant / int8 quantization for background tasks: 8–15% savings while preserving quality for non-customer-facing steps.
- Routing to cheaper region/variant for non-sensitive workloads: 5–10% incremental.

Attachments: attached a first-pass SKU estimate (paygate_pilot_sku_estimate.xlsx) and a short pilot scope we propose (redwood_pilot_scope_and_roadmap.docx).

Proposed next steps (we recommend completing by next week):
1) Sign pilot SOW (we can start a 60-day pilot after signatures). I’ll produce a draft SOW and pricing sheet by Thursday.
2) Soojin to schedule a 90-minute technical kickoff to map endpoints and identify candidate intents for caching.
3) PayGate to share (a) 7-day token histogram, (b) redacted sample prompts, (c) security questionnaire (if you have it).

Open questions from our side:
- Is the $9k/mo pilot budget palatable to procurement as a committed SKU?
- Which intents must remain 100% identical (no model variants allowed) vs. which can be candidate for quantized variants?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOW draft Thursday.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
(415) 555-0193

From: Evan Miles <evan.miles@paygate.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, PayGate Procurement <procurement@paygate.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call TCO recap — token levers, batching & caching, and pilot next steps

Thanks for the clear write-up, Ben. A couple quick clarifications before I loop in finance/procurement: 
1) That $22k/month baseline — does that include current pre- and post-processing compute we run on our side (we have a small microservice doing context enrichment)?
2) The pilot budget of $9k/mo — is that the net cost to PayGate after Redwood credits, or the gross committed spend? We’ll likely ask finance to see net liability.

I’ll pull the 7-day token histogram and a redacted sample set by EOD tomorrow. Procurement asked for an initial runbook and a simple rollback clause — can you attach a one-page fallback/rollback snippet we can show them?

Evan
Director of Product — PayGate Inc.
evan.miles@paygate.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Evan Miles <evan.miles@paygate.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call TCO recap — token levers, batching & caching, and pilot next steps

Appreciate the quick replies, Evan. Short answers below and I attached the one-page rollback/fallback snippet in the pilot doc (redwood_pilot_scope_and_roadmap.docx) for procurement. 

1) Baseline: the $22k/mo estimate is our inference endpoint spend only — it excludes your enrichment microservice CPU costs. If you want a full TCO that folds in your infra, we can run a combined model (one-off) — happy to include an ops engineer for that assessment.
2) Pilot budget: $9k/mo is presented as the net committed spend to PayGate after a one-time pilot credit Redwood applies (we’ll show gross vs. net in the SOW). We can structure the SOW with a committed SKU + overage rate that finance prefers.

A couple notes on measurable success criteria for procurement and finance: 
- Unit cost reduction (tokens/op) >= 30% measured over a 30-day rolling window.
- 95th latency <= baseline + 50ms for customer-facing intents.
- Cache hit-rate dashboard visible to PayGate team and Redwood (we’ll instrument in the kickoff).

Soojin will send a calendar invite for the technical kickoff (45–90m) with an agenda. Marissa — I’ll draft the SOW and pricing sheet and share a DocuSign link once you give the go-ahead.

—
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call TCO recap — token levers, batching & caching, and pilot next steps

Ben — thanks for the recap. Two internal notes before we send the SOW: 
- Confirming we’ll include a clause to cap PayGate’s exposure: committed SKU at $9,000/mo with a single 30-day overage window capped at 1.5x committed (to address spike risk).
- I recommend a 10% promotional credit applied up front to the pilot invoice (helps procurement sign-off).

Soojin — can you lead the kickoff and outline the top 8 intents we should instrument for caching? Let’s push the SOW draft and the DocuSign link by EOD today so Ben can get it to Evan.

Marissa Cole
